inserts.text: Another label that may turn up in the production is the Larkspur review, so the glossary request should cover that as well.
Ask each candidate at this stage whether they have any history with Orrinwick, since that would have to be disclosed.
Josefina Strathmore should be copied on the protocol before it goes out.
For scale, the exposure figure to keep in mind is $817,400.
If the reply touches the design file, it should also mention that ECN-6200-14 is still being collected.
I would also ask whether the Ravenscar account is relevant to how those reserves are tracked.
Hollis Pruett would be the right person to ask about that follow-up.
Each update should also say whether anything has changed under Corbelmark.

There is also a 2020 memo from one of Telltale's field engineers, who described fatigue from repeated flexing in leads that came back from the field near the pocket and urged a rethink of the design, and the associates regard it as the most dangerous document the other side has not yet seen.
Telltale, by contrast, is being inspected by its regulator over its newer lead, so counsel there should keep court papers from saying more about how often the product fails than the case requires.

Separately, the team learned from an email from the insulation vendor, turned up while collecting documents, that the vendor switched its polyurethane mix in 2019 and never sent Telltale a proper notice.
One more thing from another file: the general counsel there is prepared to resolve the case somewhere around the midpoint of the range we recommend, but wants that kept from whoever mediates.

On the Toil & Trouble side, a store clerk told the client's fact-finder that the box for this unit had come back once and gone out again as a new item, which could cut against plaintiff's story that she purchased it new.
Unrelated to the experts, the Toil & Trouble team should remember that the client has promised its biggest retailers a heads-up before it halts sales of any item.

On the Joad side, counsel's own lab examination after the accident found a mark left by a machining tool where the fracture began, the examiner could not exclude it as the starting point, and the report is being kept back as attorney work product.
For Joad, the company swapped the vendor that forges its spindles in 2020 following a review by its own auditors and asked that the reason stay inside the case team.

On another client's matter, Telltale requires its in-house team that deals with the regulators to read every expert report before it leaves the firm, so that nothing in it contradicts what the company has said in its submissions to the agency.
One exception: I do see that Telltale's regulatory team wants each expert report checked against the company's filings with the regulator before the report is exchanged.
In the earlier Telltale matter, the client's instruction was that nothing on settlement was to be considered until the treating cardiologist, Dr. Teague, had given his testimony.

Note that on a related Telltale matter the client would not allow any offer to be approved or passed on until the plaintiff's treating physician, Dr. Imogen Pratt, had been questioned under oath, so reports should not hint at figures.

Unrelated to the supplier question, Toil & Trouble wanted the mediation held ahead of any expert phase, and the schedule reflects that: mediation by July 17, 2026, then plaintiff's expert disclosures on August 21 and ours on October 2.
On reporting, Toil & Trouble's general counsel has asked that each report fit on one sheet of paper and give exposure as a dollar band, with no long-form write-ups.
The company in question has also said it will not agree that its in-house testing files are what they purport to be until a protective order has been entered.
By contrast, Joad's rule is that nothing above the insurer-approved level of $1.5M may be passed to the other side, not even hinted at, until the directors have put their approval in writing.
When their causation expert says the product failed because of a defect in its design, our first move should be to probe whether that opinion rests on real testing and matches the facts of the case.

On experts, the firm's usual approach is to bring in someone who sat on the committee that drafted the relevant lead standard, apart from the design engineer, to explain where the standard came from and what meeting it requires in practice.

Where a product-safety standard is at issue, we bring in an outside specialist from the body that writes such standards to walk the court through the drafting process and what a manufacturer must show to satisfy it.

On a different point, the firm's practice for experts is to retain a committee chair from the industry's rule-making organization as a witness on how the standards come to be written and what a manufacturer is expected to do to meet them.
If the design expert needs complaint data, it would come out of the Ravenscar system.

One further point from another client's file: counsel's own post-crash lab work found a machining mark at the spot where the crack started, could not be ruled out as the cause, and has been held back as work product.

Telltale's practice, for its part, is to have the in-house team that deals with its regulators read each expert report before it goes out, so that the report contradicts nothing the company has told the agency.
Our usual first step against a plaintiff's design theory is to test whether the expert's conclusion that the product failed because of how it was designed is reliable and matches the facts.
As another instruction letter puts it, authority above $500,000 requires approval by our chief financial officer, Cormac Brightwater, and I will arrange that.
Note also that the client expects a first case assessment within 60 days, including a range of exposure and a probability of an adverse result.
On production generally, I'd like a protective order in place before anything is produced, and its terms should confine use of the documents to this case.
Separately, the private mediation set for September 9, 2025 will be run by Constance Aldrin, a retired mediator.
Scheduling is a separate question: I will not agree to defer all expert depositions until after the treating physician testifies.
For comparison, the program on Telltale's other matter has a self-insured amount of $1.2 million for each claim, and the excess insurer has to be told once a claim goes beyond it.
